solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fans of Reading FC maybe with caution in the first place

indicators.note: being put in the first place means this piece goes at the front, ahead of the other

parts.note: a referee books a player when cautioning them
FC stands for Football Club

explanation.surface: Supporters of Reading Football Club get a yellow card warning first.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading FC is a real football club, which hides that 'Reading' here means the pastime of reading books.
explanation.definitionFit: A book club is a group of people who meet to discuss books, so they are keen readers.

clue.text: Conspirator grasses when picked up

indicators.note: picking something up by ear means hearing it, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: oats are cereal grasses

explanation.surface: A plotter is caught out when informers are arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grasses' suggests informers, but here it is the plants. Titus Oates fabricated the Popish Plot of 1678.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus Oates invented a Catholic plot against Charles II, making him a famous English conspirator.

clue.text: How waiter's keeping busy in Crime and Punishment

parts.note: a killing is a crime
time is a prison sentence, as in doing time

explanation.surface: Someone waiting passes the hours reading Dostoevsky's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Crime and Punishment looks like the title of the novel, but the two words are taken separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Killing time means occupying oneself idly while waiting for something, exactly what a waiter does.

clue.text: With the other hand, making good bulbs etc.

indicators.note: switching to the other hand swaps right for left, so one letter is exchanged for its opposite

parts.note: righting a wrong is making good

explanation.surface: A left-handed electrician repairs the light fittings.
explanation.walkthrough: R stands for right and L for left, so taking the other hand changes the opening R into L.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighting is the general term for bulbs, lamps and the like that illuminate a place.

clue.text: Advertising strategy devoid of ideas and such like, and too old

parts.note: a blank mind has no ideas
etc. means and so on
over age means too old for something

explanation.surface: An ad campaign is dismissed as unoriginal and dated.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads like a critique of an advertising plan, so the joining 'and' between pieces is easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Blanket coverage means advertising saturating every outlet, a sweeping media strategy.

clue.text: Fuzz stopping covert operative? That's smart

indicators.note: something stopping a gap plugs it, so this piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
nap is the fuzzy pile on cloth

explanation.surface: The police catch a secret agent, which is clever work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fuzz' is slang for the police but here means the pile on fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A snappy dresser is smart and stylish, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: In case of self-defence, file away photo

indicators.note: filing something away scatters it out of sight, so the letters are rearranged
in places this jumbled piece within the pair of outer letters
a case is the outside of something, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A lawyer files a picture as evidence in a self-defence case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' sounds legal but it marks the outside letters of self-defence.
explanation.definitionFit: A selfie is a photograph a person takes of themselves.

clue.text: Toady shaving head and beard

indicators.note: shaving off the head removes the opening letter

parts.note: to fawn is to toady

explanation.surface: A sycophant shaves his head and his beard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beard' looks like part of the shave, but it is the definition in its botanical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An awn is the bristly beard on an ear of barley or other grass.

clue.text: One starting a suit with no design, turning up fine suit

parts.note: plain fabric has no pattern

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up means the letters are read from the bottom upward

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine, and to suit is to fit

explanation.surface: A tailor makes a plain suit that fits well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' appears twice: first a lawsuit in the definition, then the verb meaning fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintiff is the party who brings a lawsuit in court.

clue.text: Male keeping a learner in detention here?

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: a stag is a male deer
taken as written
L is the learner-driver plate

explanation.surface: A man keeps a schoolboy in after class.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests school detention; the definition is a place of imprisonment, signalled by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp, where captives were held in detention.

clue.text: Providing oxygen, say, also supply nitrogen at first

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, it means bending freely, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter only

parts.note: initial letter, also its chemical symbol
oxygen is an example of a gas

explanation.surface: A chemist offers to supply oxygen as well as nitrogen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' reads as a verb, but as the adverb from supple it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: As long as is a conjunction meaning on condition that, just as providing does.

clue.text: Wine's two appealing qualities when knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back means turned the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal
SA is short for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A wine's two attractions show when it is drunk down.
explanation.walkthrough: Both IT and SA are long-standing crossword terms for sex appeal. 'Knocked back' suggests downing a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine from Piedmont.

clue.text: Rook was forced to capture knight, giving control

parts.note: to rook someone is to swindle or take them in

indicators.note: capturing something takes it prisoner, so it is held inside

parts.note: had to means was forced to
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A chess move: the rook must take the knight, gaining command of the board.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture misleads: 'Rook' is the verb meaning to cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something in hand is to assume control of it.

clue.text: Person tidying Barnet Hospital, bearing furniture item

parts.note: H is the map symbol for hospital
an air is a manner or bearing
a dresser is a kitchen cupboard with shelves

explanation.surface: Someone tidies up Barnet Hospital while carrying a piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is a London borough with a real hospital, but it is also Cockney rhyming slang: Barnet Fair means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdresser cuts and styles hair, so tidies a person's Barnet.

clue.text: Cook bean, admitting it's disgusting for a snack

indicators.note: admitting someone lets them in, so this piece goes inside

parts.note: to do food is to cook it
bean and nut are both slang for the head
an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Cooking beans produces something revolting as a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bean' looks like food but means the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A doughnut is a fried sweet dough ring, a typical snack.

clue.text: A doner mostly very bad? It's just in need of cooking

indicators.note: something bad has gone wrong, so the letters are scrambled
mostly keeps all but the final letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written before trimming
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doner kebab is mostly awful, and it still needs cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very' sits between 'mostly' and 'bad' as if an adverb, but it is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Oven-ready food is prepared and needs only to be cooked.

clue.text: Current teacher's retiring, one controlling a pupil?

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: pupils call a male teacher sir

explanation.surface: The present teacher is retiring, after keeping pupils in line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pupil' sounds like a schoolchild, matching the teacher; here it is the opening in the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is the coloured ring of the eye whose muscles widen or narrow the pupil.

clue.text: Shady criminal with uncertainty over time period in work

indicators.note: criminal means crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order
in a down entry over places the earlier pieces above the last one

parts.note: the five letters rearranged
an if is a doubt or uncertainty
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A dodgy character is unsure how long he has been inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Period' and 'time' suggest a prison stretch; the definition is a working shift.
explanation.definitionFit: A day shift is the daytime period of work in a factory or hospital rota.

clue.text: Supplier of good fare from India, guided westwards

indicators.note: in an across entry westwards means right to left, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: I is India in the phonetic alphabet
led means guided

explanation.surface: Fine food arrives from India, brought west.
explanation.walkthrough: The geography suggests an Indian import; India is only a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling fine prepared foods.

clue.text: Switch positions from time to time

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the two settings of a switch

explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch positions' reads like an instruction to move, but it names the settings marked on a switch.
explanation.definitionFit: A switch has on and off settings, and the phrase on and off also means occasionally, at irregular intervals.

clue.text: Countenance gossip about getting stuck into struggle

indicators.note: getting stuck into something means going inside it

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: gas is idle chatter

explanation.surface: Tolerate gossip about joining a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Countenance' looks like a verb meaning tolerate, but it is the noun for face.
explanation.definitionFit: A visage is a person's face, which is also what countenance means as a noun.

clue.text: Nonchalance from barbers oddly accepting on-line issues

indicators.note: accepting something takes it in, so the other piece goes inside
oddly keeps the letters in odd-numbered positions

parts.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters
e-zines are magazines published online

explanation.surface: Barbers casually take internet complaints in their stride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issues' suggests problems; here it means editions of magazines.
explanation.definitionFit: Breeziness is a relaxed, carefree manner, the same quality as nonchalance.

clue.text: Having been hurt, back in love

indicators.note: back means turned the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a sore spot has been hurt

explanation.surface: Someone who was hurt is falling for another again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back in love' reads as a phrase, but 'back' is the turnaround and 'love' alone the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, and his name stands for erotic love itself.

clue.text: Liberal punching old Tory moderate in hooter

parts.note: O is short for old

indicators.note: a fist punching into something goes inside it

parts.note: wets were moderate Conservatives under Thatcher
L abbreviates Liberal

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician hits an elderly moderate Conservative on the nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooter' is British slang for nose, but here it means an owl; a wet was Thatcher's term for a moderate Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is a young owl, a small hooter, since owls are named for their hooting call.

clue.text: View Greek and Hindu deities with nothing between them

indicators.note: the plural names gods, telling the solver both the Greek and Hindu words are names of gods
placing a piece between two others sets it in the middle of the row

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
O looks like zero
Rama is a Hindu deity, an avatar of Vishnu

explanation.surface: A sight of Greek and Hindu gods with nothing separating them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deities' serves both names: one Greek god, one Hindu god.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide, unbroken view of a landscape.

clue.text: Portion of sorbet or an antiquated mince pie?

indicators.note: a portion is a slice, so the letters are a run taken from inside the next word

parts.note: the second to fourth letters

explanation.surface: Choosing dessert: some sorbet, or an old-fashioned mince pie?
explanation.walkthrough: Mince pies is Cockney rhyming slang for eyes, and orb is an old poetic word for an eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Orb is a literary, dated word for the eye, which a mince pie means in rhyming slang.

clue.text: Visiting Asian capital, we hear one may be in Oxford

indicators.note: we hear means the words are judged by their sound when spoken

parts.note: visiting means being in, and Seoul is the capital of South Korea

explanation.surface: A traveller in Seoul learns of someone who may be at Oxford University.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford looks like the university, but it is a type of laced leather shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: An insole is the inner sole lining a shoe, so one sits inside an Oxford shoe.

clue.text: I'm off, needing a couple of runs

parts.note: in cricket a bye is a run scored when the ball passes the batter untouched
the second of the pair

explanation.surface: A batsman says he is going, needing just two more runs.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket scores byes as extras when the ball beats both batter and keeper; two of them make the farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Bye-bye is a casual farewell said by someone leaving.

clue.text: With soldiers invading, being in a complete state

indicators.note: invaders force their way in, so this piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an entity is a being
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Troops invade, taking over a whole country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' suggests a nation under attack, but it means a condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Entirety is the condition of being whole and complete.
